outcomes.outcome: the node is configured as a member of the domain and joined (its machine account works and the DC holds it)
domain users and groups resolve on the node through nsswitch and winbind
pam_winbind requires membership of the listed groups, and the openvpn PAM file is installed

a domain user in a listed group logs in through PAM (login, the service openvpn_server's plugin uses) with the domain password, with the domain prefix and by the bare name (winbind use default domain); a wrong password and a domain user outside the listed groups are refused

Kerberos: the default realm is the domain's realm (the NetBIOS name and the tld, upper-case as AD realms are), and the only realm stanza is the template's literal DOMAIN.LOCAL, so a Kerberos client finds the DC's KDC through DNS; kinit for a domain user without naming a realm gets a ticket, also with a lowercase tld parameter. Nothing in the class's login path uses Kerberos (security = domain joins over RPC; pam_winbind's krb5_auth stays off); the [logging] section is read by a KDC, which the node does not run

host names also resolve through NetBIOS/WINS (nsswitch's hosts line ends in wins; smb.conf names the DC as the WINS server): the DC's NetBIOS name resolves through the wins source to the address DNS gives its FQDN, and an unknown name does not
